bull_bear.body:
- Deep expertise in applied chemistry — decades of application and process knowledge across textiles, home and personal care, industrial cleaning, water treatment, construction, paints and coatings, paper and pulp, rubber, and dyes & pigments, enabling customised formulations
- Integrated and flexible manufacturing — ability to produce key intermediates in-house and run scalable, customised small-to-medium batches with rapid formulation adjustment across liquid and powder chemistries
- Long-standing customer relationships — 200+ domestic and 20+ international customers as of 31st March 2026, across multiple industries and geographies
- In-house R&D and application development laboratory at Moraiya, Ahmedabad, focused on formulation enhancement, process optimisation and bio-based alternatives
- Established sales and distribution network — over 50 authorised distributors across India plus direct exports, backed by a sales and marketing team of 16 employees
- Portfolio breadth and diversification — 350+ products marketed under over 35 proprietary brands across four segments, reducing dependence on any single end-use sector
- Internationally recognised quality, environmental and occupational safety certifications plus a zero liquid discharge facility, supporting access to compliance-sensitive customers
- Exclusive distribution rights across India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka for a Netherlands-based technology partner's fluorine-free, bio-based repellent technologies for textile and construction applications
- Experienced leadership team with expertise in specialty chemicals, manufacturing, business development and human capital management
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Unrealised government subsidy receivable recognised on an accrual basis — The auditors draw attention by way of Emphasis of Matter to a subsidy receivable of ₹485.40 lakhs (including ₹248.40 lakhs pertaining to the current year and ₹237.00 lakhs pertaining to earlier years) recognised over the last three financial years, which remained unrealised as at March 31, 2026. Ultimate realisation depends on approval and disbursement by the concerned Government authorities, so a sizeable accrued asset sits outside the Company's control.
- Counterparty insolvency exposure on trade receivables — A second Emphasis of Matter flags receivables of ₹27.97 lakhs recoverable from M/s Morarjee Textiles Limited, against whom insolvency proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 were initiated; recoverability depends on the outcome of the resolution process. It illustrates the credit exposure inherent in a customer base concentrated in cyclical processing industries.
- Cyber fraud and internal financial control weakness — Subsequent to the year end the Company was the target of a third-party cyber fraud on 20th and 21st July 2026, through which ₹147.72 lakhs was fraudulently caused to be paid out; ₹52.46 lakhs has been recovered and a further ₹99.55 lakhs traced and placed on hold by the banks. The incident was reported to the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and the Company is strengthening internal financial controls and cyber-security systems to prevent recurrence — a live control-environment risk for a newly listed company.
- Credit risk on trade receivables — The Board's report identifies credit risk arising from trade receivables in the normal course of business, mitigated through periodic assessment of customer creditworthiness, a diversified customer base across industries and geographies, and continuous monitoring — but the exposure is structural to the working-capital-heavy specialty chemicals model.
- Liquidity and funding risk — Liquidity risk relates to the Company's ability to meet financial obligations and operational funding requirements in a timely manner; it is managed through adequate cash balances and access to committed credit facilities, and availability of financing is separately listed as a factor that could influence operations.
- Raw material price, energy cost and supply chain volatility — Geopolitical developments — tensions in West Asia and the continuing Russia-Ukraine conflict — drove volatility in crude oil and commodity prices, elevated freight and input costs, periodic supply disruptions and trade delays, particularly for industries dependent on imported raw materials and integrated global supply chains. Fluctuations in raw material prices are explicitly named in the cautionary statement as a factor that could cause actual results to differ.
- Tightening environmental and chemical regulation — Stricter standards relating to industrial emissions, PFAS compounds, volatile organic compounds and wastewater management are reshaping the specialty chemicals industry, forcing continued investment in environmentally compliant formulations, bio-based feedstock and advanced treatment technologies; regulatory developments are also listed among the factors that could influence the Company's operations.
- Demand, competitive and foreign exchange exposure flagged in the cautionary statement — The forward-looking cautionary statement enumerates changes in economic conditions, industry dynamics, changes in demand patterns, competitive pressures and foreign exchange movements as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially — relevant given a business selling into cyclical textile and industrial end-markets with an export footprint of around 5% of revenue across 12 countries.

business.body: Neochem Bio Solutions Ltd is a specialty performance chemicals company with a legacy spanning more than four decades, manufacturing a diversified portfolio of over 350 customised formulations across four product segments: polymers, surfactants, silicones, and esters and bio-based sustainable solutions. Its products act as critical inputs for textiles and garment processing, home and personal care, institutional and industrial cleaning, water treatment, paints and coatings, paper and pulp, construction, rubber, and dyes and pigments. It serves a diversified domestic and international customer base through direct engagement and an extensive distribution network, supported by in-house R&D and application research that drive customer-specific formulation development.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Polymers:** Acrylic emulsions and polymers, Dispersants and rheological modifiers, Polyamine flocculants, Polymeric surfactants, Softening agents, EVENOL, AMPINOL, DYFAST, KOLAPSOL, PRIMAPRINT, TRUTONE, BRILLOPRINT, AMBITAC, AQUATREAT
- **Surfactants:** Personal care surfactants for shampoos, face washes and cleansers, Homecare surfactants for dishwashing liquids, detergents and surface cleaners, Institutional cleaning solutions, KLARIZYM, KLARITOL, QUNOX, LUBIMAX, NEUTRAX, MERCOL, FABSAFE
- **Silicones:** Amino-silicone softeners, Hydrophilic emulsions, Slip- and mar-resistance additives for architectural paints, Anti-foams for high-temperature dyeing and wastewater treatment, GLIDEX, PRESTOFIN
- **Esters and Bio-based Sustainable Solutions:** Plant-based softeners (Vegan Ester Quats), Natural clay-based scouring agents, REVLION, ASTASOFT
- **Other portfolio lines:** Textile processing auxiliaries for pre-treatment, dyeing, finishing, printing and coating, Anti-foaming agents, Water-treatment anti-scalants, dispersants, de-colourants and flocculants, Green Essentials portfolio: vegan softeners, phosphate-free chelating agents, corn glucose-based surfactants
business.title: Products & brands

- Long-standing customer relationships — 200+ domestic and 20+ international customers as of 31st March 2026, across multiple industries and geographies

- Established sales and distribution network — over 50 authorised distributors across India plus direct exports, backed by a sales and marketing team of 16 employees
- Portfolio breadth and diversification — 350+ products marketed under over 35 proprietary brands across four segments, reducing dependence on any single end-use sector
- Internationally recognised quality, environmental and occupational safety certifications plus a zero liquid discharge facility, supporting access to compliance-sensitive customers
- Exclusive distribution rights across India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka for a Netherlands-based technology partner's fluorine-free, bio-based repellent technologies for textile and construction applications
- Experienced leadership team with expertise in specialty chemicals, manufacturing, business development and human capital management
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Diversify beyond a textile-focused base into home & personal care, paints & coatings, water treatment, construction, paper, rubber and industrial cleaning, with Home & Personal Care called out as a key growth driver after rising from 2% of revenue in FY 2023-24 to 14% in FY 2025-26
- Expand the portfolio of bio-based and environmentally responsible formulations as sustainability reshapes customer demand, including newly introduced platforms FabBrite, Ampinol and Avakote
- Keep innovation central via the dedicated R&D and application development centre — customer-centric formulations, process efficiency improvements, bio-based chemistries and import-substitute products for niche performance chemical applications
- Deepen the collaboration with Lamoral Coatings of the Netherlands to bring advanced fluorine-free technologies to the Indian market as industries transition to PFAS-free chemistries
- Pursue calibrated international expansion — products currently reach customers across 12 countries with exports at around 5% of revenue — by building technical expertise, regulatory compliance and enduring customer relationships
- Advance sustainable manufacturing practices and process efficiencies to minimise environmental footprint while maintaining standards of quality, safety, governance and ethical conduct
- As a newly listed company, focus on innovation, expanding high-potential segments, strengthening global presence and improving operational efficiency
- Maintain a strengthened capital structure after the IPO, whose proceeds were applied to debt reduction, to retain financial flexibility for future growth opportunities
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no new capex project, capacity addition or commissioning timeline. Manufacturing is at Saket Industrial Estate, Moraiya, Sanand, Ahmedabad (a strategically located production facility in Gujarat), with an installed production capacity of 22,000 MTPA spanning 6,763 square metres, partially automated and configured for small to medium batches across liquid and powder-based chemistries, plus dedicated warehousing of approximately 1,350 metric tonnes of raw materials and finished goods. Installed capacity has been unchanged at 22,000 MT across 2024, 2025 and 2026, so growth has come from filling existing capacity rather than adding it: actual production rose from 7,694 MT to 9,200 MT and then to 11,589 MT, lifting capacity utilisation from 35.0% to 41.8% and then to 52.7%, which leaves roughly half the installed base as headroom. Expansion is therefore framed as application and geography breadth rather than tonnage — a diversification-led strategy broadening the portfolio beyond textiles into home and personal care, institutional and industrial cleaning, water treatment, paints and coatings and construction chemicals; strengthening presence across Asia, Oceania, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and selected African and Middle Eastern markets; a network of 50+ authorised distributors; exclusive distribution rights across India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka from a Netherlands-based technology partner for fluorine-free, bio-based repellent technologies; and continued investment in the dedicated R&D and application development centre and the in-house QC/QA laboratory at the Moraiya site, which operates on a Zero Liquid Discharge basis. The Directors' Report states only that prudent liquidity management and access to committed credit facilities support day-to-day operations, capital requirements and business expansion initiatives, without naming a project or a rupee quantum. The Capital Commitments named disclosure supplied in this bundle is truncated at its caption ('Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on Capital') and carries no figure, so no capex quantum is recorded.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for high-performance, application-oriented chemicals is increasing across construction chemicals, electronic chemicals, water treatment additives, adhesives, coatings and specialty polymers
- Growing investments in electric vehicles, semiconductor manufacturing, renewable energy infrastructure and lightweight materials are expected to support demand for specialised chemical formulations over the coming years
- Industry growth supported by rising infrastructure investments and increasing localisation of manufacturing supply chains
- Stricter standards on industrial emissions, PFAS compounds, VOC and wastewater management are accelerating adoption of environmentally compliant formulations, bio-based feedstock, advanced treatment technologies and waterborne chemistries
- Global specialty chemicals market projected to expand from approximately $1.26 trillion in 2026 to nearly $1.54 trillion by 2031, a CAGR of 4.09% (Mordor Intelligence)
- India's specialty chemicals market valued at approximately $67 billion in 2025 and projected to reach nearly $93.4 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 3.65% over 2026-2034 (Mordor Intelligence)
- Indian real GDP projected to expand in the range of 6.8% to 7.2% in FY 2027, supported by domestic consumption, infrastructure investment and increasing manufacturing activity
- Global GDP projected at 3.1% in 2026 improving to 3.2% in 2027, with headline inflation rising to 4.4% in 2026 before easing to 3.7% in 2027 — a backdrop of elevated freight and input costs and periodic supply disruption
- Management notes the sector is shifting towards sustainable, application-driven solutions, positioning customised formulations, bio-based chemistries and responsible manufacturing as the demand lever

open.item: Continue a diversification-led growth strategy that broadens the application portfolio beyond textiles into home and personal care, institutional and industrial cleaning, water treatment, paints and coatings, and construction chemicals to reduce concentration risk and balance the revenue mix.

Develop sustainable alternatives under the Green Essentials portfolio, including vegan softeners, phosphate-free chelating agents and corn glucose-based surfactants, through in-house R&D and application laboratories.

Introduce differentiated fluorine-free, bio-based repellent technologies for textile and construction applications under exclusive distribution rights across India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka from a Netherlands-based technology partner.

Strengthen international presence across Asia, Oceania, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and selected African and Middle Eastern markets through customised formulations meeting regional performance and regulatory requirements.

Continue to improve resource efficiency through initiatives relating to water conservation, energy optimisation and emission reduction while operating the manufacturing facility on a zero liquid discharge approach.
Grow the Home & Personal Care business further as a key growth driver for the years ahead, having taken it from 2% of revenue in FY 2023-24 to 14% in FY 2025-26.

Continue calibrated international expansion beyond the current reach of 12 countries, where exports account for around 5% of revenue, by building technical expertise, regulatory compliance and customer relationships.

Leverage the strengthened collaboration with Lamoral Coatings of the Netherlands to introduce advanced fluorine-free technologies to the Indian market as industries transition towards PFAS-free chemistries.
Focus R&D on customer-centric formulations, process efficiencies, bio-based chemistries and import-substitute products for niche performance chemical applications.
Expand the bio-based and environmentally responsible formulation portfolio, having introduced the FabBrite, Ampinol and Avakote platforms during the year.

risks.note: The auditors draw attention by way of Emphasis of Matter to a subsidy receivable of ₹485.40 lakhs (including ₹248.40 lakhs pertaining to the current year and ₹237.00 lakhs pertaining to earlier years) recognised over the last three financial years, which remained unrealised as at March 31, 2026. Ultimate realisation depends on approval and disbursement by the concerned Government authorities, so a sizeable accrued asset sits outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Counterparty insolvency exposure on trade receivables
risks.note: A second Emphasis of Matter flags receivables of ₹27.97 lakhs recoverable from M/s Morarjee Textiles Limited, against whom insolvency proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 were initiated; recoverability depends on the outcome of the resolution process. It illustrates the credit exposure inherent in a customer base concentrated in cyclical processing industries.

risks.risk: Cyber fraud and internal financial control weakness
risks.note: Subsequent to the year end the Company was the target of a third-party cyber fraud on 20th and 21st July 2026, through which ₹147.72 lakhs was fraudulently caused to be paid out; ₹52.46 lakhs has been recovered and a further ₹99.55 lakhs traced and placed on hold by the banks. The incident was reported to the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and the Company is strengthening internal financial controls and cyber-security systems to prevent recurrence — a live control-environment risk for a newly listed company.

The Board's report identifies credit risk arising from trade receivables in the normal course of business, mitigated through periodic assessment of customer creditworthiness, a diversified customer base across industries and geographies, and continuous monitoring — but the exposure is structural to the working-capital-heavy specialty chemicals model.

Liquidity risk relates to the Company's ability to meet financial obligations and operational funding requirements in a timely manner; it is managed through adequate cash balances and access to committed credit facilities, and availability of financing is separately listed as a factor that could influence operations.

risks.risk: Raw material price, energy cost and supply chain volatility
risks.note: Geopolitical developments — tensions in West Asia and the continuing Russia-Ukraine conflict — drove volatility in crude oil and commodity prices, elevated freight and input costs, periodic supply disruptions and trade delays, particularly for industries dependent on imported raw materials and integrated global supply chains. Fluctuations in raw material prices are explicitly named in the cautionary statement as a factor that could cause actual results to differ.

Stricter standards relating to industrial emissions, PFAS compounds, volatile organic compounds and wastewater management are reshaping the specialty chemicals industry, forcing continued investment in environmentally compliant formulations, bio-based feedstock and advanced treatment technologies; regulatory developments are also listed among the factors that could influence the Company's operations.

risks.risk: Demand, competitive and foreign exchange exposure flagged in the cautionary statement
risks.note: The forward-looking cautionary statement enumerates changes in economic conditions, industry dynamics, changes in demand patterns, competitive pressures and foreign exchange movements as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially — relevant given a business selling into cyclical textile and industrial end-markets with an export footprint of around 5% of revenue across 12 countries.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A specialty performance chemicals manufacturer of over 350 customised formulations across polymers, surfactants, silicones and esters & bio-based sustainable solutions, sold into textiles, home & personal care, industrial cleaning, water treatment and coatings.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Neochem Bio Solutions Ltd is a specialty performance chemicals company with a legacy spanning more than four decades, manufacturing a diversified portfolio of over 350 customised formulations across four product segments: polymers, surfactants, silicones, and esters and bio-based sustainable solutions. Its products act as critical inputs for textiles and garment processing, home and personal care, institutional and industrial cleaning, water treatment, paints and coatings, paper and pulp, construction, rubber, and dyes and pigments. It serves a diversified domestic and international customer base through direct engagement and an extensive distribution network, supported by in-house R&D and application research that drive customer-specific formulation development.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Polymers:** Acrylic emulsions and polymers, Dispersants and rheological modifiers, Polyamine flocculants, Polymeric surfactants, Softening agents, EVENOL, AMPINOL, DYFAST, KOLAPSOL, PRIMAPRINT, TRUTONE, BRILLOPRINT, AMBITAC, AQUATREAT
- **Surfactants:** Personal care surfactants for shampoos, face washes and cleansers, Homecare surfactants for dishwashing liquids, detergents and surface cleaners, Institutional cleaning solutions, KLARIZYM, KLARITOL, QUNOX, LUBIMAX, NEUTRAX, MERCOL, FABSAFE
- **Silicones:** Amino-silicone softeners, Hydrophilic emulsions, Slip- and mar-resistance additives for architectural paints, Anti-foams for high-temperature dyeing and wastewater treatment, GLIDEX, PRESTOFIN
- **Esters and Bio-based Sustainable Solutions:** Plant-based softeners (Vegan Ester Quats), Natural clay-based scouring agents, REVLION, ASTASOFT
- **Other portfolio lines:** Textile processing auxiliaries for pre-treatment, dyeing, finishing, printing and coating, Anti-foaming agents, Water-treatment anti-scalants, dispersants, de-colourants and flocculants, Green Essentials portfolio: vegan softeners, phosphate-free chelating agents, corn glucose-based surfactants

end_markets.body:

- Personal care
- Institutional and industrial cleaning

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for high-performance, application-oriented chemicals is increasing across construction chemicals, electronic chemicals, water treatment additives, adhesives, coatings and specialty polymers
- Growing investments in electric vehicles, semiconductor manufacturing, renewable energy infrastructure and lightweight materials are expected to support demand for specialised chemical formulations over the coming years
- Industry growth supported by rising infrastructure investments and increasing localisation of manufacturing supply chains
- Stricter standards on industrial emissions, PFAS compounds, VOC and wastewater management are accelerating adoption of environmentally compliant formulations, bio-based feedstock, advanced treatment technologies and waterborne chemistries
- Global specialty chemicals market projected to expand from approximately $1.26 trillion in 2026 to nearly $1.54 trillion by 2031, a CAGR of 4.09% (Mordor Intelligence)
- India's specialty chemicals market valued at approximately $67 billion in 2025 and projected to reach nearly $93.4 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 3.65% over 2026-2034 (Mordor Intelligence)
- Indian real GDP projected to expand in the range of 6.8% to 7.2% in FY 2027, supported by domestic consumption, infrastructure investment and increasing manufacturing activity
- Global GDP projected at 3.1% in 2026 improving to 3.2% in 2027, with headline inflation rising to 4.4% in 2026 before easing to 3.7% in 2027 — a backdrop of elevated freight and input costs and periodic supply disruption
- Management notes the sector is shifting towards sustainable, application-driven solutions, positioning customised formulations, bio-based chemistries and responsible manufacturing as the demand lever

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Diversify beyond a textile-focused base into home & personal care, paints & coatings, water treatment, construction, paper, rubber and industrial cleaning, with Home & Personal Care called out as a key growth driver after rising from 2% of revenue in FY 2023-24 to 14% in FY 2025-26
- Expand the portfolio of bio-based and environmentally responsible formulations as sustainability reshapes customer demand, including newly introduced platforms FabBrite, Ampinol and Avakote
- Keep innovation central via the dedicated R&D and application development centre — customer-centric formulations, process efficiency improvements, bio-based chemistries and import-substitute products for niche performance chemical applications
- Deepen the collaboration with Lamoral Coatings of the Netherlands to bring advanced fluorine-free technologies to the Indian market as industries transition to PFAS-free chemistries
- Pursue calibrated international expansion — products currently reach customers across 12 countries with exports at around 5% of revenue — by building technical expertise, regulatory compliance and enduring customer relationships
- Advance sustainable manufacturing practices and process efficiencies to minimise environmental footprint while maintaining standards of quality, safety, governance and ethical conduct
- As a newly listed company, focus on innovation, expanding high-potential segments, strengthening global presence and improving operational efficiency
- Maintain a strengthened capital structure after the IPO, whose proceeds were applied to debt reduction, to retain financial flexibility for future growth opportunities

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no new capex project, capacity addition or commissioning timeline. Manufacturing is at Saket Industrial Estate, Moraiya, Sanand, Ahmedabad (a strategically located production facility in Gujarat), with an installed production capacity of 22,000 MTPA spanning 6,763 square metres, partially automated and configured for small to medium batches across liquid and powder-based chemistries, plus dedicated warehousing of approximately 1,350 metric tonnes of raw materials and finished goods. Installed capacity has been unchanged at 22,000 MT across 2024, 2025 and 2026, so growth has come from filling existing capacity rather than adding it: actual production rose from 7,694 MT to 9,200 MT and then to 11,589 MT, lifting capacity utilisation from 35.0% to 41.8% and then to 52.7%, which leaves roughly half the installed base as headroom. Expansion is therefore framed as application and geography breadth rather than tonnage — a diversification-led strategy broadening the portfolio beyond textiles into home and personal care, institutional and industrial cleaning, water treatment, paints and coatings and construction chemicals; strengthening presence across Asia, Oceania, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and selected African and Middle Eastern markets; a network of 50+ authorised distributors; exclusive distribution rights across India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka from a Netherlands-based technology partner for fluorine-free, bio-based repellent technologies; and continued investment in the dedicated R&D and application development centre and the in-house QC/QA laboratory at the Moraiya site, which operates on a Zero Liquid Discharge basis. The Directors' Report states only that prudent liquidity management and access to committed credit facilities support day-to-day operations, capital requirements and business expansion initiatives, without naming a project or a rupee quantum. The Capital Commitments named disclosure supplied in this bundle is truncated at its caption ('Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on Capital') and carries no figure, so no capex quantum is recorded.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deep expertise in applied chemistry — decades of application and process knowledge across textiles, home and personal care, industrial cleaning, water treatment, construction, paints and coatings, paper and pulp, rubber, and dyes & pigments, enabling customised formulations
- Integrated and flexible manufacturing — ability to produce key intermediates in-house and run scalable, customised small-to-medium batches with rapid formulation adjustment across liquid and powder chemistries
- Long-standing customer relationships — 200+ domestic and 20+ international customers as of 31st March 2026, across multiple industries and geographies
- In-house R&D and application development laboratory at Moraiya, Ahmedabad, focused on formulation enhancement, process optimisation and bio-based alternatives
- Established sales and distribution network — over 50 authorised distributors across India plus direct exports, backed by a sales and marketing team of 16 employees
- Portfolio breadth and diversification — 350+ products marketed under over 35 proprietary brands across four segments, reducing dependence on any single end-use sector
- Internationally recognised quality, environmental and occupational safety certifications plus a zero liquid discharge facility, supporting access to compliance-sensitive customers
- Exclusive distribution rights across India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka for a Netherlands-based technology partner's fluorine-free, bio-based repellent technologies for textile and construction applications
- Experienced leadership team with expertise in specialty chemicals, manufacturing, business development and human capital management
